claims.text: RiskMandate's Agent Behaviour Policy is written before an agent runs, in four words: reach, mandate, gap and barriers.
claims.quote: RiskMandate's four words are reach, mandate, gap and barriers.

claims.text: The article proposes two more words for the policy, footprint and blast radius, new to the policy and not to the industry.
claims.quote: This article proposes two more.

claims.text: As of 2 October 2026 the founders are still reviewing the proposal; until decided with the RiskMandate team it is an idea published on sgit.ai, not a change to the policy.
claims.quote: the founders are still reviewing this proposal, and the best way to make it happen will be decided with the RiskMandate team

claims.text: A barrier is typed as a boundary, a setting, an expectation or nothing; only the boundary is a control, and most of what organisations call controls turn out to be expectations once typed.
claims.quote: Only the boundary is a control, and most of what organisations call controls turn out to be expectations once they are typed.

claims.text: The Kit Bag plan typed the barriers for a browser extension before any code and found thirteen rows in the gap, four stopped by the platform and the rest by nothing but the code as written.
claims.quote: found thirteen rows in the gap, four of them stopped by the platform and the rest by nothing but the code as written

value.unit: rows in the gap, four stopped by the platform

claims.text: The footprint is the set of things the agent actually did, in a period, read from the record afterwards; it is evidence, not a decision.
claims.quote: The footprint is the set of things the agent actually did, in a period, read from the record afterwards.

claims.text: The footprint comes from the connector's audit log, the model's tool-call record, a connector twin, a vault's commit history and append lanes, and the agent's own messages in files.
claims.quote: A vault's commit history. Every agent on this site that works in a vault leaves a signed, versioned record of every file it touched

claims.text: Reading rather than intercepting makes the footprint passive, needing no production access, and accumulating, so some findings only exist at the twelfth week.
claims.quote: It is passive: nothing sits inline, nothing adds latency, nothing can break the agent by being there.

claims.text: Footprint in the gap, an action within the reach and outside the mandate that nothing stopped, is a near miss, the most valuable finding because it arrives before the damage.
claims.quote: In the safety disciplines this is a near miss, and it is the most valuable kind of finding there is, because it arrives before the damage.

claims.text: A dormant mandate is a row the owner asked for that the footprint never shows: the mandate was over-stated, a check never ran, or the agent cannot do it.
claims.quote: A row the owner asked for that the footprint never shows.

claims.text: Each mandate row wants a hint of how often the owner expects to see it, always, sometimes, rarely or hopefully never, so a dormant row can be told from a contingency.
claims.quote: So each mandate row wants a hint of how often the owner expects to see it, always, sometimes, rarely, hopefully never

claims.text: Footprint outside the reach should be impossible by construction, so when it appears the reach inventory is wrong, a finding about the measurement.
claims.quote: This should be impossible by construction, so when it appears, the reach inventory is wrong

claims.text: Attempts a boundary stopped are the footprint of the barriers; an expectation by definition has no hits because nothing was there to record the stop.
claims.quote: An expectation, by definition, has no hits, because nothing was there to record the stop.

claims.text: Read the footprint for a month and you have the mandate as practised, the fastest honest way to write a policy for an agent that has none.
claims.quote: Read the footprint for a month and you have the mandate as practised

claims.text: Of the ten agents that grew in eight days, six have a written policy, and the footprint is how the other four get one.
claims.quote: Six of them have a written policy; the footprint is how the other four get one

claims.text: Blast radius is not a sixth set but a measure attached to a row: what it would cost the business if that row were used in full, today.
claims.quote: what it would cost the business if that row were used in full, today

claims.text: Blast radius is defined over the reach, not the mandate, because an attacker who takes an agent over through a prompt injection inherits its reach and ignores its mandate.
claims.quote: inherits the agent's reach and ignores its mandate entirely

claims.text: Blast radius is about the business, not the system, which is why it connects the policy to the risk register rather than the infrastructure diagram.
claims.quote: This is why blast radius connects the policy to the risk register rather than to the infrastructure diagram

claims.text: Potential blast radius is computed from the reach before the agent runs; realised blast radius is what the footprint touched; they should converge as the policy matures.
claims.quote: Potential blast radius is computed from the reach, before the agent runs

claims.text: Blast radius has a second axis the industry usually leaves out: whether there is a way back.
claims.quote: It has a second axis: whether there is a way back.

claims.text: The same footprint carries a different blast radius on different days: a staging table dropped three times is the same row, and the review on the incident day can say this is not the first time.
claims.quote: the review on day forty-one can say something that is otherwise impossible to say: this is not the first time

claims.text: AWS IAM Access Analyzer added unused-access findings in November 2023 and from June 2024 recommends a refined policy from access activity.
claims.quote: added unused-access findings in November 2023

claims.text: Google Cloud's role recommendations compare a principal's permissions with those used in the last ninety days and will not recommend removing one that was used.
claims.quote: compare a principal's permissions with those used in the last ninety days

claims.text: Microsoft's Permission Creep Index scores granted against exercised permissions weighted by damage, and its report found workload identities using under five per cent of what they were granted.
claims.quote: found workload identities using under five per cent of what they were granted

value.unit: per cent of granted permissions used, upper bound

claims.text: The cloud tools cannot do the other half: there is no mandate in an IAM policy, so no dormant mandate and no near miss, only an identity using a permission; the owner's intent is what the policy adds.
claims.quote: There is no mandate in an IAM policy, so there is no such thing as a dormant mandate

claims.text: A vault is a footprint recorder by construction: every commit signed, versioned and append-only, every lane message recorded, and a read key lets a reviewer read it without touching anything.
claims.quote: The first is that a vault is a footprint recorder by construction.

claims.text: Barriers shrink the reach; containment and reversibility shrink the blast radius, and most of what sgit does for agents is shrink the irreversible part of it.
claims.quote: Barriers shrink the reach. Containment and reversibility shrink the blast radius, and they are different levers.

claims.text: The honest status is a proposal with the pieces in place and the worked example still to do; reading the ten agents' footprint against six policies will be the second article.
claims.quote: The honest status is that this is a proposal with the pieces in place and the worked example still to do.

claims.text: The owner expects the near misses to be mostly mandate gaps rather than misbehaviour, and that at least one check written into a policy has never fired.
claims.quote: at least one check we wrote into a policy has never fired

claims.text: The brief to the RiskMandate team asks for five things: a footprint section, an expected-use hint on every mandate row, blast radius on every gap row, the mandate as practised as a view, and a review cadence.
claims.quote: The brief to the RiskMandate team asks for five things, in this order of usefulness

claims.text: The review cadence is monthly for a new agent and quarterly once the potential and realised readings have converged.
claims.quote: Monthly for a new agent, quarterly once the potential and the realised readings have converged.

claims.text: The four figures are illustrative, an inbox agent with placeholder capabilities and counts and a staging table nobody owns, and the industry references were checked on 2 October 2026.
claims.quote: The four figures are illustrative: an inbox agent with placeholder capabilities and counts, and a staging table that nobody owns.

claims.text: Earlier pages called the reach the grant and the gap the delta; they are the same things, and the connector twin is the cleanest footprint recorder because it sits where the actions cross the line.
claims.quote: called the reach the grant and the gap the delta; they are the same things
